title: Why Did the Resistor Burn? Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav uses exactly the right resistor value, yet a few seconds later the resistor is too hot to touch and smells burnt. The value was correct, so what went wrong? In this animated lesson we learn to read component specifications and the datasheet every part comes with: description and features, absolute maximum ratings, electrical characteristics with minimum, typical and maximum values, graphs and the package.

We pick out the key specs of resistors, capacitors and inductors and see what a 5 percent tolerance really means. On a live breadboard the supply across a 1 kilo ohm, quarter watt resistor is turned up while the oscilloscope and readout show voltage, current and power together, until the power crosses the rating. We derive P = V^2/R = I^2R and the largest safe voltage and current, work out the limits for Aarav's resistor, and read a derating curve. All datasheet values shown are example figures for a generic part. Then the exam trap (absolute maximum is not a working value), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 33 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 4: Passive Electronic Components (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
